Read a brain surface mesh

Source: R/read_surface_mesh.R
read_surface_mesh.Rd

Reads a surface file into a mesh that describes itself: vertices, faces, and a ggseg.formats::mesh_space() recording the vertex space, hemisphere and relationship to a standard space.

Usage

read_surface_mesh(
  path,
  space,
  face_index_base = 0L,
  format = c("auto", "freesurfer", "gifti")
)

Arguments

path

Path to a FreeSurfer binary surface or a GIFTI surface file.

space

A ggseg.formats::mesh_space() describing what the mesh's coordinates mean.

face_index_base

0L or 1L – what the returned face indices should count from.

format

Source format. "auto" reads the extension, which is why it can be overridden: a FreeSurfer surface is often named lh.inflated, with no extension to go on.

Value

A mesh from ggseg.formats::brain_mesh(), carrying mesh_space and face_index_base attributes.

Details

Meshes are independent of atlases. An atlas defines regions – labels and the vertex indices they cover – while a mesh is a surface to draw them on. The two meet only at vertex_space: an atlas's indices mean something on a mesh in the space the atlas was built against, and nothing on any other. This function therefore produces a mesh, never an atlas, and nothing here feeds the create_*_from_*() pipelines.

face_index_base chooses what the returned faces count from. FreeSurfer surfaces are read as 1-based and GIFTI as 0-based, so a base is always converted to rather than assumed, and ggseg.formats::brain_mesh() checks the result. The ecosystem genuinely holds both conventions – ggseg.formats inflated surfaces are 0-based, ggseg.meshes cortical surfaces are 1-based – because four build scripts each chose independently. Choosing here, once, is the point.

FreeSurfer surfaces are read through mris_convert where it is available, which handles the QUAD surfaces mri_tessellate writes, falling back to freesurferformats.

Examples

if (FALSE) {
space <- ggseg.formats::mesh_space(
  vertex_space = "fsaverage5",
  hemi = "left",
  anatomical = FALSE,
  surface = "inflated"
)
read_surface_mesh(
  file.path(Sys.getenv("FREESURFER_HOME"), "subjects", "fsaverage5",
            "surf", "lh.inflated"),
  space = space
)
}
